subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded submanifold is the range of the derivative of any local representation
subproblems.statement: Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a local representation of N ⊆ ℝ^P in the sense of Simon Ch. 2 §4 (4.1): V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ of class C^r on V with r ≥ 1, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V the tangent space T_{ψ(v)}N = {γ'(0) : γ ∈ C¹((−1,1); ℝ^P), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = ψ(v)} (tangentSpace N (ψ v)) equals the range of Dψ(v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → v ∈ V → tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v)

Used by the new child local_plane (step 1: Dψ(v)a ∈ T_{ψ(v)}M for every chart point v). The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (definition of T_yM for an embedded submanifold, and its identification with Dψ(ℝ^d)); used in steps 3 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. Setup. Put y := ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ N and L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v; since V is open and r ≥ 1, ψ is differentiable at v with derivative L. L is injective, so (finite dimension) there is c > 0 with |Lh| ≥ c|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d; range L is a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. range L ⊆ T_yN. Let w = La. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y works (y ∈ N). Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(v, ρ) ⊆ V and κ > 0 with κ|a| < ρ, and let σ(s) := κ·tanh(s/κ), a smooth function with σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and |σ(s)| < κ. Put γ(s) := ψ(v + σ(s)a). Then v + σ(s)a ∈ V for all s, so γ is C^r (in particular C¹) on ℝ ⊇ (−1,1), γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = y, and γ'(0) = Dψ(v)(σ'(0)a) = La = w. Hence w ∈ T_yN.
3. Embedding property. If z_k ∈ V and ψ(z_k) → y then z_k → v: the set K := {ψ(z_k) : k} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact and contains every z_k; any cluster point z ∈ V of (z_k) satisfies ψ(z) = y = ψ(v) by continuity, so z = v by injectivity on V; hence z_k → v.
4. T_yN ⊆ range L. Let w ∈ T_yN, witnessed by γ. As γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, there is s_0 ∈ (0,1) with γ(s) ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V) for |s| < s_0; write γ(s) = ψ(β(s)) with β(s) ∈ V (unique by injectivity). By step 3 (applied along sequences s_k → 0), β(s) → v as s → 0.
5. Write ψ(z) − y = L(z − v) + ρ(z) with |ρ(z)| ≤ η(|z − v|)·|z − v|, η(t) → 0 as t → 0. For |s| small, η(|β(s) − v|) ≤ c/2, hence |γ(s) − y| ≥ c|β(s) − v| − (c/2)|β(s) − v|, i.e. |β(s) − v| ≤ (2/c)|γ(s) − y|. Since γ is differentiable at 0, |γ(s) − y| ≤ C|s| for small |s|; thus |β(s) − v| = O(|s|) and |ρ(β(s))| = o(|s|).
6. Hence (γ(s) − y)/s = L((β(s) − v)/s) + o(1), so the difference quotients lie within o(1) of range L. Letting s → 0, w = γ'(0) belongs to the closure of range L, which is range L. Together with step 2, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v).
proof_key_steps: Curves s ↦ ψ(v + σ(s)a) with σ smooth, bounded, σ'(0) = 1 show range Dψ(v) ⊆ T_{ψ(v)}N.
Properness and injectivity make ψ^{-1} continuous at ψ(v) along N ∩ W.
Injectivity of Dψ(v) gives |β(s) − v| = O(|γ(s) − ψ(v)|), so difference quotients of any curve in N lie in range Dψ(v) up to o(1).

subproblems.title: Chart localization: N ∩ B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ ψ(V ∩ B_ε(v₀)) and is compact, for a proper injective chart
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N, W ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^d, ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P and v₀ ∈ V. Assume W is open, ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for every ε > 0 there is ρ > 0 such that B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ W, N ∩ B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ ψ(V ∩ B_ε(v₀)), and N ∩ B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) is compact.

This child is the accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_ret_chart_localization of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.retraction-a1.chart_localization-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 7d0e7d04f4a8; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). It is the precise form of the remark in the supplied proof of the parent (Submission.codim1_hcp_flat_cone_is_plane) that the chart ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto the relatively open set W ∩ M and maps open subsets of V onto relatively open subsets of M: near ψ(v₀), every point of M is ψ of a point of V close to v₀. Used by the new child local_plane (step 4). The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim; in it, 'the parent proof' refers to that node's own parent.

Source: steps 1 and 4(a) of the parent proof, written out directly with compact sets. Those steps say: ψ|_V : V → W ∩ N is a homeomorphism because ψ is proper into W, so ψ⁻¹ is continuous at y; and N ∩ B̄_{ρ₁} = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_{ρ₁})) is compact. Put y := ψ(v₀); all balls in ℝ^P below are centred at y.
1. y ∈ W, because y = ψ(v₀) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ N. As W is open, there is ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ W (take half the radius of an open ball about y contained in W).
2. K₀ := B̄_{ρ₀}(y) is compact (closed balls of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P are compact) and K₀ ⊆ W. So C₀ := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K₀) is compact by the properness hypothesis. Hence C := C₀ ∖ B_ε(v₀) is compact, being a compact set minus an open set.
3. C ⊆ V and ψ is continuous on V, so ψ(C) is compact, hence closed in ℝ^P.
4. y ∉ ψ(C). Indeed, suppose c ∈ C and ψ(c) = y = ψ(v₀). Then c = v₀, because c, v₀ ∈ V and ψ is injective on V. But v₀ ∈ B_ε(v₀) since ε > 0, whereas c ∉ B_ε(v₀).
5. By steps 3–4, the complement of ψ(C) is an open set containing y. So there is ρ₂ > 0 with B_{ρ₂}(y) ∩ ψ(C) = ∅. Put ρ := min(ρ₀, ρ₂/2) > 0. Then B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ B̄_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ W and B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ B_{ρ₂}(y), so B̄_ρ(y) ∩ ψ(C) = ∅.
6. Inclusion. Let z ∈ N ∩ B̄_ρ(y). Then z ∈ W by step 5, so z ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V): z = ψ(v) with v ∈ V. Since ψ(v) = z ∈ B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ K₀, we have v ∈ C₀. If v ∉ B_ε(v₀), then v ∈ C and z = ψ(v) ∈ ψ(C) ∩ B̄_ρ(y) = ∅, which is impossible. Hence v ∈ V ∩ B_ε(v₀) and z ∈ ψ(V ∩ B_ε(v₀)).
7. Compactness. We claim N ∩ B̄_ρ(y) = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(y))). '⊆': as in step 6, z = ψ(v) with v ∈ V and ψ(v) ∈ B̄_ρ(y). '⊇': if v ∈ V and ψ(v) ∈ B̄_ρ(y), then ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ N ⊆ N. Since B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ W is compact, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(y)) is compact by properness. Its image under ψ, which is continuous on this subset of V, is compact.
8. Steps 5–7 give ρ > 0 with all three required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: y = ψ(v₀) ∈ W; choose B̄_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ W; by properness C := (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_{ρ₀}(y))) ∖ B_ε(v₀) is compact.
ψ(C) is compact and misses y by injectivity of ψ on V, so some B̄_ρ(y) with ρ ≤ ρ₀ misses ψ(C).
Each z ∈ N ∩ B̄_ρ(y) is ψ(v) with v ∈ (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_{ρ₀}(y))) ∖ C, so v ∈ B_ε(v₀).
N ∩ B̄_ρ(y) = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(y))) is compact by properness and continuity of ψ on V.

subproblems.title: A C¹ immersion of an open subset of ℝ^m into an m-dimensional subspace has relatively open image (parent step 4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let H ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim H = m (Module.finrank ℝ H = m), let B ⊆ ℝ^m be open and let ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on B, with Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v injective for every v ∈ B and ψ(B) ⊆ H. Then there is an open set O ⊆ ℝ^P with O ∩ H = ψ(B); that is, ψ(B) is relatively open in H.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (H : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (B : Set (Euclid m)) (ψ : Euclid m → Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ H = m → IsOpen B → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ B → (∀ v ∈ B, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ v)) → ψ '' B ⊆ (H : Set (Euclid P)) → ∃ O : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen O ∧ O ∩ (H : Set (Euclid P)) = ψ '' B
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 4 of the supplied proof of the parent (Submission.codim1_hcp_flat_cone_is_plane): "By the inverse function theorem (applied to ψ|_B as a C¹ map into H_c ≅ ℝ^m), ψ|_B is an open map into H_c, so ψ(B) is an open subset of H_c". Here it is proved for an arbitrary open B and an arbitrary m-dimensional subspace H, with the fact that Dψ(v) maps into H derived from ψ(B) ⊆ H. Book anchor: Simon, Appendix B, Theorem B.2 (book/chapter-B.txt lines 37–39); the printed proof ends with '|A|² ≡ 0 on M' (line 282) and leaves the passage from |A| ≡ 0 to a hyperplane implicit; the parent's supplied proof makes that passage explicit, and this child carries out part of it.

1. Notation. Regard H as a finite-dimensional real inner product space, hence complete, with the norm and topology induced from ℝ^P; write ι : H → ℝ^P for the inclusion. Let π : ℝ^P → H be the orthogonal projection onto H (Mathlib: H.orthogonalProjectionOnto). π is continuous and linear, and π(h) = h for every h ∈ H (Mathlib: Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_mem_subspace_eq_self). Put g := π ∘ ψ : ℝ^m → H. Since ψ(B) ⊆ H, ι(g(v)) = ψ(v) for every v ∈ B.

2. Strict differentiability. Fix v ∈ B. B is open and ψ is C¹ on B, so ψ is C¹ on a neighbourhood of v and therefore strictly differentiable at v with strict derivative L := Dψ(v) (Mathlib: ContDiffOn.contDiffAt, then ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt with 1 ≠ 0). π is continuous linear, so by the chain rule g is strictly differentiable at v with strict derivative π ∘ L.

3. L takes values in H. The map ι ∘ π ∘ ψ coincides with ψ on B (step 1), and B is a neighbourhood of v. By the chain rule ι ∘ π ∘ ψ is differentiable at v with derivative ι ∘ π ∘ L. Two functions that agree on a neighbourhood of v have the same derivative at v, so L = ι ∘ π ∘ L. Hence La = π(La) ∈ H for every a ∈ ℝ^m.

4. π ∘ L is a linear isomorphism ℝ^m → H. If π(La) = π(Lb), then La = π(La) = π(Lb) = Lb by step 3, and a = b because L = Dψ(v) is injective (hypothesis, v ∈ B). So π ∘ L is injective. dim ℝ^m = m = dim H, so the injective linear map π ∘ L : ℝ^m → H is also surjective (rank–nullity; Mathlib: LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank). Hence π ∘ L is a linear bijection, and, the spaces being finite-dimensional, a continuous linear equivalence E_v : ℝ^m ≃ H (Mathlib: LinearEquiv.ofBijective, then LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv). By step 2, g has strict derivative E_v at v.

5. Inverse function theorem. ℝ^m is complete and g has the invertible strict derivative E_v at v, so g maps the neighbourhood filter of v onto the neighbourhood filter of g(v) in H (Mathlib: HasStrictFDerivAt.map_nhds_eq_of_equiv). B is a neighbourhood of v, so g(B) is a neighbourhood of g(v) in H.

6. g(B) is open in H. Every point of g(B) has the form g(v) with v ∈ B, and g(B) is a neighbourhood of it by step 5. Hence g(B) is an open subset of H. By the definition of the subspace topology there is an open set O ⊆ ℝ^P such that, for h ∈ H, ι(h) ∈ O if and only if h ∈ g(B) (Mathlib: isOpen_induced_iff).

7. O ∩ H = ψ(B). (⊆) Let y ∈ O ∩ H. Regarded as an element of H, y lies in g(B) by step 6, so y = ι(g(v)) for some v ∈ B, and ι(g(v)) = ψ(v) by step 1. So y ∈ ψ(B). (⊇) Let y = ψ(v) with v ∈ B. Then y ∈ H by hypothesis. As an element of H, y equals g(v) by step 1, and g(v) ∈ g(B), so y ∈ O by step 6. Thus y ∈ O ∩ H.

8. O is open and O ∩ H = ψ(B), which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: g := π ∘ ψ, with π the orthogonal projection onto H, agrees with ψ on B; since ψ = ι ∘ π ∘ ψ near v, Dψ(v) takes values in H.
π ∘ Dψ(v) is injective, hence, as dim ℝ^m = m = dim H, a continuous linear equivalence ℝ^m ≃ H, and g has this strict derivative at v.
Inverse function theorem: g(B) is a neighbourhood of each g(v), so g(B) is open in H.
The subspace topology gives an open O ⊆ ℝ^P with O ∩ H = ψ(B).

subproblems.title: A linear subspace of dimension at least 2 with the origin removed is connected (parent step 6)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let H ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim H ≥ 2 (2 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ H). Then H ∖ {0} is connected, i.e. nonempty and preconnected.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (H : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 2 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ H → IsConnected ((H : Set (Euclid P)) \ {0})
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 6 of the supplied proof of the parent (Submission.codim1_hcp_flat_cone_is_plane): "H_c ∖ {0} is connected because dim H_c = m ≥ 2 (a real vector space of dimension ≥ 2 minus a point is path-connected)". Mathlib's isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Connected.lean) is outside the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, so an elementary argument with convex half-spaces is given. ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product, |·| the Euclidean norm, and K := H ∖ {0}. Book anchor: Simon, Appendix B, Theorem B.2 (book/chapter-B.txt lines 37–39); the printed proof ends with '|A|² ≡ 0 on M' (line 282) and leaves the passage from |A| ≡ 0 to a hyperplane implicit; the parent's supplied proof makes that passage explicit, and this child carries out part of it.

1. Half-spaces of H. For v ∈ ℝ^P put C_v := {x ∈ H : ⟨v, x⟩ > 0}. C_v is the intersection of the subspace H (a convex set) with the open half-space {x : ⟨v, x⟩ > 0} (convex, because x ↦ ⟨v, x⟩ is linear), so C_v is convex and hence preconnected (Mathlib: Convex.isPreconnected). C_v ⊆ K, because ⟨v, 0⟩ = 0 is not positive. For x ≠ 0, ⟨x, x⟩ = |x|² > 0.

2. K is nonempty. H ≠ {0}, since dim H ≥ 2 > 0 = dim {0}. Choose x₀ ∈ H with x₀ ≠ 0. Then x₀ ∈ K, and x₀ ∈ C_{x₀} by step 1.

3. A nonzero w ∈ H orthogonal to x₀. Let L := (span{x₀})^⊥. dim span{x₀} = 1 (x₀ ≠ 0) and dim span{x₀} + dim L = P, so dim L = P − 1. By the dimension formula, dim(H + L) + dim(H ∩ L) = dim H + dim L (Mathlib: Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq), and dim(H + L) ≤ P. Hence dim(H ∩ L) ≥ dim H + (P − 1) − P = dim H − 1 ≥ 1, so H ∩ L ≠ {0}. Choose w ∈ H ∩ L with w ≠ 0. Then w ∈ H and ⟨x₀, w⟩ = ⟨w, x₀⟩ = 0.

4. T := C_{x₀} ∪ C_w ∪ C_{−x₀} is preconnected. First, x₀ + w ∈ H, ⟨x₀, x₀ + w⟩ = |x₀|² + 0 > 0 and ⟨w, x₀ + w⟩ = 0 + |w|² > 0, so x₀ + w ∈ C_{x₀} ∩ C_w. The union of two preconnected sets with a common point is preconnected (Mathlib: IsPreconnected.union), so C_{x₀} ∪ C_w is preconnected. Second, −x₀ + w ∈ H, ⟨w, −x₀ + w⟩ = 0 + |w|² > 0 and ⟨−x₀, −x₀ + w⟩ = |x₀|² − 0 > 0, so −x₀ + w ∈ C_w ∩ C_{−x₀} ⊆ (C_{x₀} ∪ C_w) ∩ C_{−x₀}. Hence T is preconnected.

5. For every y ∈ K, C_y meets T. Note y ∈ H and y ≠ 0. If ⟨x₀, y⟩ > 0, then y ∈ C_y ∩ C_{x₀}, because ⟨y, y⟩ > 0. If ⟨x₀, y⟩ < 0, then ⟨−x₀, y⟩ > 0 and y ∈ C_y ∩ C_{−x₀}. If ⟨x₀, y⟩ = 0, then x₀ + y ∈ H, ⟨y, x₀ + y⟩ = 0 + |y|² > 0 and ⟨x₀, x₀ + y⟩ = |x₀|² + 0 > 0, so x₀ + y ∈ C_y ∩ C_{x₀}.

6. K is preconnected. Fix y ∈ K. By steps 4 and 5, T ∪ C_y is a union of two preconnected sets with a common point, hence preconnected. It is contained in K (step 1), contains x₀ (x₀ ∈ C_{x₀} ⊆ T) and contains y (y ∈ C_y, as ⟨y, y⟩ > 0). So every point of K lies, together with the fixed point x₀, in a preconnected subset of K. This implies that K is preconnected (Mathlib: isPreconnected_of_forall).

7. By steps 2 and 6, K = H ∖ {0} is nonempty and preconnected, i.e. connected. ∎
proof_key_steps: The half-spaces C_v = {x ∈ H : ⟨v, x⟩ > 0} are convex, hence preconnected, and lie in H ∖ {0}.
dim H ≥ 2 gives x₀ ≠ 0 in H and, by the dimension formula, w ≠ 0 in H with ⟨x₀, w⟩ = 0.
C_{x₀} ∪ C_w ∪ C_{−x₀} is preconnected (common points x₀ + w and −x₀ + w), and every C_y with y ∈ H ∖ {0} meets it.
Every y ∈ H ∖ {0} lies with x₀ in a preconnected subset of H ∖ {0}, so H ∖ {0} is connected.

subproblems.title: Near each point, a flat C¹ hypercone of A₀ coincides with an m-dimensional subspace of A₀ (parent steps 1, 3, 4)
subproblems.statement: Local flatness. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P; ν : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Hypotheses: dim A₀ = m + 1; M ⊆ A₀; M is an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M); tx ∈ M for every x ∈ M and t > 0; ν is differentiable at every x ∈ M; for every x ∈ M, ν(x) ∈ A₀, |ν(x)| = 1 and ν(x)·v = 0 for every v ∈ tangentSpace M x; and Dν(x)v = 0 (fderiv ℝ ν x v = 0) for every x ∈ M and v ∈ tangentSpace M x. Conclusion: for every x ∈ M there are a linear subspace H ⊆ A₀ with dim H = m and an open set O ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ O and O ∩ M = O ∩ H.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (A₀ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P → Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ A₀ = m + 1 → M ⊆ (A₀ : Set (Euclid P)) → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M → (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∀ x ∈ M, t • x ∈ M) → (∀ x ∈ M, DifferentiableAt ℝ ν x) → (∀ x ∈ M, ν x ∈ A₀ ∧ ‖ν x‖ = 1 ∧ ∀ v ∈ tangentSpace M x, inner ℝ (ν x) v = 0) → (∀ x ∈ M, ∀ v ∈ tangentSpace M x, fderiv ℝ ν x v = 0) → ∀ x ∈ M, ∃ H : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ H = m ∧ H ≤ A₀ ∧ ∃ O : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen O ∧ x ∈ O ∧ O ∩ M = O ∩ (H : Set (Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 1, 3 and 4 of the supplied proof of the parent (Submission.codim1_hcp_flat_cone_is_plane), carried out on one chart ball around the given point x: zero tangential derivative makes ν, and then z ↦ ν(x)·z, constant on the chart image (step 1 and the first half of step 3); the cone rays force the constant to be 0 (second half of step 3, used here only for t near 1); the inverse function theorem makes the chart image open in the plane (step 4). Siblings used: chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv), chart_localization (Submission.dor_lmb_ret_chart_localization) and immersion_open (Submission.codim1_hcp_fcp_immersion_image_open_in_subspace). ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product, T_y := tangentSpace M y, B_ρ and B̄_ρ are open and closed balls. Book anchor: Simon, Appendix B, Theorem B.2 (book/chapter-B.txt lines 37–39); the printed proof ends with '|A|² ≡ 0 on M' (line 282) and leaves the passage from |A| ≡ 0 to a hyperplane implicit; the parent's supplied proof makes that passage explicit, and this child carries out part of it.

Fix x ∈ M.

1. Chart. Apply IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M at y = x: there are an open V ⊆ ℝ^m, an open W ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ W, and ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P with ψ of class C¹ on V, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Since x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), choose v₀ ∈ V with ψ(v₀) = x. V is open, so choose δ > 0 with B := B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V. For v ∈ V: ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M, so ψ(v) ∈ M; ψ is differentiable at v (C¹ on the open set V); and chart_tangent_space (with N = M, d = m, r = 1 ≥ 1 and the chart data above) gives T_{ψ(v)} = range Dψ(v). In particular Dψ(v)a ∈ T_{ψ(v)} for every a ∈ ℝ^m.

2. ν ∘ ψ is constant on B. Let v ∈ B. ν is differentiable at ψ(v) ∈ M (hypothesis) and ψ is differentiable at v (step 1), so by the chain rule ν ∘ ψ is differentiable at v and D(ν ∘ ψ)(v)a = Dν(ψ(v))(Dψ(v)a) for a ∈ ℝ^m. Since ψ(v) ∈ M and Dψ(v)a ∈ T_{ψ(v)} (step 1), the flatness hypothesis gives Dν(ψ(v))(Dψ(v)a) = 0. So ν ∘ ψ is differentiable on B with zero derivative at every point of B. B is open and convex, hence preconnected, so ν ∘ ψ is constant on B (mean value theorem; Mathlib: IsOpen.is_const_of_fderiv_eq_zero). Since v₀ ∈ B and ψ(v₀) = x, ν(ψ(v)) = ν(x) =: n for every v ∈ B.

3. ψ(B) lies in an affine hyperplane. Let f(v) := ⟨n, ψ(v)⟩. For v ∈ B, f is differentiable at v with Df(v)a = ⟨n, Dψ(v)a⟩, by the chain rule for the continuous linear functional ⟨n, ·⟩. By step 2, n = ν(ψ(v)). By step 1, Dψ(v)a ∈ T_{ψ(v)}, and ψ(v) ∈ M. So the normality hypothesis at ψ(v) gives Df(v)a = ⟨ν(ψ(v)), Dψ(v)a⟩ = 0. As in step 2, f is constant on B: ⟨n, ψ(v)⟩ = ⟨n, ψ(v₀)⟩ = ⟨n, x⟩ for every v ∈ B.

4. Localization. Apply chart_localization with N = M, the open set W, the set V, the map ψ (continuous on V, being C¹ there), which is injective on V with ψ(V) = W ∩ M and has the compactness property of step 1, the point v₀ ∈ V and ε = δ > 0. It gives ρ > 0 with M ∩ B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ ψ(V ∩ B_δ(v₀)). Since ψ(v₀) = x and B_δ(v₀) = B ⊆ V, this says M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ ψ(B).

5. ⟨n, x⟩ = 0 (cone property). Put s := ρ/(|x| + 1) > 0 and t := 1 + s > 0. Then |tx − x| = |sx| = s|x| ≤ s(|x| + 1) = ρ, so tx ∈ B̄_ρ(x). Also tx ∈ M by the cone hypothesis (t > 0, x ∈ M). By step 4, tx = ψ(v) for some v ∈ B. Step 3 gives t⟨n, x⟩ = ⟨n, tx⟩ = ⟨n, ψ(v)⟩ = ⟨n, x⟩, that is, s⟨n, x⟩ = 0. As s ≠ 0, ⟨n, x⟩ = 0. With step 3: ⟨n, ψ(v)⟩ = 0 for every v ∈ B.

6. The plane H. n ∈ A₀ and |n| = 1 by the normality hypothesis at x, so n ≠ 0. Let H := A₀ ∩ (span{n})^⊥, a linear subspace with H ⊆ A₀. Dimension: span{n} ⊆ A₀ and span{n} + (span{n})^⊥ = ℝ^P (orthogonal decomposition; Mathlib: Submodule.sup_orthogonal_of_hasOrthogonalProjection), so A₀ + (span{n})^⊥ = ℝ^P has dimension P. dim span{n} = 1 and dim span{n} + dim (span{n})^⊥ = P, so dim (span{n})^⊥ = P − 1. The dimension formula dim(A₀ + (span{n})^⊥) + dim(A₀ ∩ (span{n})^⊥) = dim A₀ + dim (span{n})^⊥ (Mathlib: Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq) reads P + dim H = (m + 1) + (P − 1), so dim H = m. Moreover ψ(B) ⊆ H: for v ∈ B, ψ(v) ∈ M ⊆ A₀, and ⟨n, ψ(v)⟩ = 0 by step 5, i.e. ψ(v) ∈ (span{n})^⊥.

7. ψ(B) is open in H. Apply immersion_open to H (dim H = m, step 6), the open ball B, and ψ: ψ is C¹ on B because B ⊆ V; Dψ(v) is injective for v ∈ B ⊆ V; and ψ(B) ⊆ H by step 6. It gives an open O' ⊆ ℝ^P with O' ∩ H = ψ(B).

8. Conclusion. Let O := B_ρ(x) ∩ O', an open set. x ∈ O: x ∈ B_ρ(x) as ρ > 0, and x = ψ(v₀) ∈ ψ(B) = O' ∩ H ⊆ O'. O ∩ M ⊆ O ∩ H: if y ∈ O ∩ M, then y ∈ M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ ψ(B) ⊆ H by steps 4 and 6. O ∩ H ⊆ O ∩ M: if y ∈ O ∩ H, then y ∈ O' ∩ H = ψ(B), so y = ψ(v) with v ∈ B ⊆ V, and y ∈ M by step 1. Hence O ∩ M = O ∩ H, where H ⊆ A₀ is a linear subspace with dim H = m, O is open and x ∈ O. Since x ∈ M was arbitrary, the statement is proved. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take a chart ψ with ψ(v₀) = x and a ball B = B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V; chart_tangent_space gives Dψ(v)a ∈ T_{ψ(v)}M.
Chain rule and flatness: D(ν∘ψ) = 0 on B, so ν∘ψ ≡ n := ν(x) (mean value theorem); then normality gives D⟨n, ψ⟩ = 0, so ⟨n, ψ(v)⟩ = ⟨n, x⟩ on B.
chart_localization gives ρ > 0 with M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ ψ(B); the cone point (1 + s)x lies there, forcing ⟨n, x⟩ = 0.
H := A₀ ∩ n^⊥ has dimension m (dimension formula) and contains ψ(B); immersion_open gives an open O' with O' ∩ H = ψ(B).
O := B_ρ(x) ∩ O' satisfies x ∈ O and O ∩ M = O ∩ H.

subproblems.title: A punctured set that is locally an m-plane of the (m+1)-space A₀ is a punctured m-plane (parent steps 2, 5–8)
subproblems.statement: Globalization. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P. Hypotheses: m ≥ 2; dim A₀ = m + 1; M ≠ ∅; 0 ∉ M; closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0}; and for every x ∈ M there are a linear subspace H ⊆ A₀ with dim H = m and an open set O ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ O and O ∩ M = O ∩ H. Conclusion: there is a linear subspace H₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with dim H₀ = m (Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m) and M = H₀ ∖ {0}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (A₀ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (M : Set (Euclid P)), 2 ≤ m → Module.finrank ℝ A₀ = m + 1 → M.Nonempty → (0 : Euclid P) ∉ M → closure M ⊆ insert 0 M → (∀ x ∈ M, ∃ H : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ H = m ∧ H ≤ A₀ ∧ ∃ O : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen O ∧ x ∈ O ∧ O ∩ M = O ∩ (H : Set (Euclid P))) → ∃ H₀ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m ∧ M = (H₀ : Set (Euclid P)) \ {0}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 2 and 5–8 of the supplied proof of the parent (Submission.codim1_hcp_flat_cone_is_plane). The supplied proof shows that each connected component M_c of M is open and closed in H_c ∖ {0}, which is connected because m ≥ 2, so M_c = H_c ∖ {0}, and that two different planes would meet away from 0 by a dimension count in A₀. Here a component M_c is replaced by U_H ∩ M, where U_H is the union of all open sets on which M agrees with H. This is the same clopen argument and the same dimension count, without local connectedness or connected components. (Remark, not used in the proof: in the parent's terms U_H ∩ M is the union of the components M_c with H_c = H, so step 3 below is the parent's steps 4–6 for that union and step 5 below is the parent's step 7.) Sibling used: punctured_connected (Submission.codim1_hcp_fcp_punctured_subspace_isConnected). "Subspace" means linear subspace of ℝ^P, and B_ε(y) is an open ball. Book anchor: Simon, Appendix B, Theorem B.2 (book/chapter-B.txt lines 37–39); the printed proof ends with '|A|² ≡ 0 on M' (line 282) and leaves the passage from |A| ≡ 0 to a hyperplane implicit; the parent's supplied proof makes that passage explicit, and this child carries out part of it.

1. Uniqueness of local planes. Claim: let y ∈ M, let H₁, H₂ be subspaces and O₁, O₂ open sets with y ∈ O₁ ∩ O₂, O₁ ∩ M = O₁ ∩ H₁ and O₂ ∩ M = O₂ ∩ H₂. Then H₁ = H₂. By symmetry it suffices to show H₁ ⊆ H₂. Since y ∈ O₁ ∩ M = O₁ ∩ H₁ and y ∈ O₂ ∩ M = O₂ ∩ H₂, y ∈ H₁ and y ∈ H₂. Let h ∈ H₁. O₁ ∩ O₂ is open and contains y, so B_ε(y) ⊆ O₁ ∩ O₂ for some ε > 0. Put s := ε/(2(|h| + 1)) > 0 and z := y + sh. Then |z − y| = s|h| < ε, so z ∈ O₁ ∩ O₂. Also z ∈ H₁, as y, h ∈ H₁. Hence z ∈ O₁ ∩ H₁ = O₁ ∩ M, so z ∈ M. Then z ∈ O₂ ∩ M = O₂ ∩ H₂, so z ∈ H₂. Therefore sh = z − y ∈ H₂ and h = s⁻¹(sh) ∈ H₂.

2. The maximal agreement set. For a subspace H let U_H be the union of all open sets O ⊆ ℝ^P with O ∩ M = O ∩ H. Then: (i) U_H is open; (ii) every open O with O ∩ M = O ∩ H satisfies O ⊆ U_H; (iii) U_H ∩ M = U_H ∩ H, since a point of U_H lies in some member O of the union, and O ∩ M = O ∩ H.

3. Claim: if dim H ≥ 2 and U_H ∩ M ≠ ∅, then H ∖ {0} ⊆ U_H. Let K := H ∖ {0}, which is connected by punctured_connected. Let G := ℝ^P ∖ closure(U_H ∩ M), an open set.
 (a) K ⊆ U_H ∪ G. Let z ∈ K. If z ∉ closure(U_H ∩ M), then z ∈ G. Otherwise z ∈ closure(U_H ∩ M) ⊆ closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0} and z ≠ 0, so z ∈ M. By hypothesis there are a subspace H_z and an open O_z with z ∈ O_z and O_z ∩ M = O_z ∩ H_z. O_z is an open neighbourhood of a point of closure(U_H ∩ M), so it contains some y ∈ U_H ∩ M. Apply step 1 at y ∈ M to the open sets U_H ∋ y (with U_H ∩ M = U_H ∩ H by 2(iii)) and O_z ∋ y (with O_z ∩ M = O_z ∩ H_z): H = H_z. So O_z ∩ M = O_z ∩ H, hence O_z ⊆ U_H by 2(ii), and z ∈ U_H.
 (b) K ∩ U_H ∩ G = ∅. If z ∈ K ∩ U_H, then z ∈ U_H ∩ H = U_H ∩ M ⊆ closure(U_H ∩ M) by 2(iii), so z ∉ G.
 (c) U_H and G are open, and K is preconnected. By (a) and (b), K ⊆ U_H or K ⊆ G (Mathlib: isPreconnected_iff_subset_of_disjoint). Pick y₀ ∈ U_H ∩ M. Then y₀ ∈ U_H ∩ H by 2(iii), and y₀ ≠ 0 because 0 ∉ M, so y₀ ∈ K. But y₀ ∈ U_H ∩ M ⊆ closure(U_H ∩ M), so y₀ ∉ G. Hence K ⊄ G, and therefore K ⊆ U_H.

4. The plane H₀. Since M ≠ ∅, pick x₀ ∈ M. By hypothesis there are a subspace H₀ ⊆ A₀ with dim H₀ = m and an open O₀ with x₀ ∈ O₀ and O₀ ∩ M = O₀ ∩ H₀. By 2(ii), O₀ ⊆ U_{H₀}, so x₀ ∈ U_{H₀} ∩ M. As dim H₀ = m ≥ 2, step 3 gives H₀ ∖ {0} ⊆ U_{H₀}. Consequently H₀ ∖ {0} ⊆ U_{H₀} ∩ H₀ = U_{H₀} ∩ M ⊆ M, using 2(iii).

5. M ⊆ H₀ ∖ {0}. Let y ∈ M. By hypothesis there are a subspace H_y ⊆ A₀ with dim H_y = m and an open O_y with y ∈ O_y and O_y ∩ M = O_y ∩ H_y. As in step 4, y ∈ U_{H_y} ∩ M and H_y ∖ {0} ⊆ U_{H_y}. Dimension count: H₀ + H_y ⊆ A₀, so dim(H₀ + H_y) ≤ dim A₀ = m + 1. The dimension formula gives dim(H₀ + H_y) + dim(H₀ ∩ H_y) = dim H₀ + dim H_y = 2m (Mathlib: Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq). Hence dim(H₀ ∩ H_y) ≥ 2m − (m + 1) = m − 1 ≥ 1. So H₀ ∩ H_y ≠ {0}, and there is w ∈ H₀ ∩ H_y with w ≠ 0. Then w ∈ H₀ ∖ {0} ⊆ U_{H₀} (step 4) and w ∈ H_y ∖ {0} ⊆ U_{H_y}. Also w ∈ U_{H₀} ∩ H₀ = U_{H₀} ∩ M, so w ∈ M. Step 1 at w, with the open sets U_{H₀} and U_{H_y} and the identities 2(iii), gives H₀ = H_y. Finally y ∈ O_y ∩ M = O_y ∩ H_y, so y ∈ H_y = H₀, and y ≠ 0 because 0 ∉ M. Thus y ∈ H₀ ∖ {0}.

6. Conclusion. By steps 4 and 5, M = H₀ ∖ {0}, and dim H₀ = m (Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m). ∎
proof_key_steps: Two local plane pairs (H₁, O₁), (H₂, O₂) at the same point y ∈ M have H₁ = H₂ (move from y along h ∈ H₁ inside O₁ ∩ O₂).
U_H := ⋃{O open : O ∩ M = O ∩ H} is open with U_H ∩ M = U_H ∩ H, and contains every such O.
If dim H ≥ 2 and U_H ∩ M ≠ ∅, then U_H and the complement of closure(U_H ∩ M) separate the connected set H ∖ {0}; closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0} and uniqueness give the covering, so H ∖ {0} ⊆ U_H.
For H₀ from a point x₀ ∈ M, H₀ ∖ {0} ⊆ M. For any y ∈ M the planes H₀ and H_y share some w ≠ 0 (dimension count in A₀), so uniqueness at w gives H_y = H₀ and y ∈ H₀ ∖ {0}.
